sources.entry: Aman Check - Dated, honest condition report for a used Mac: locks, battery, SSD and guided hardware tests. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/MidZai/aman_check) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: Aman Check is a free, open-source native macOS app that produces a dated, plain-language condition report for a used Mac, covering locks, battery, SSD health, sensors and guided hardware tests.
summary.what_it_does: It runs on the Mac being sold and reads locks and blockers (Activation Lock, Apple Account count, MDM, firmware password, SIP, FileVault, security chip), battery cycles and capacity, internal SSD S.M.A.R.T. data, configuration, and fan and temperature sensors without changing anything on the machine. It then walks the person through guided tests of the display, keyboard, trackpad, speakers, microphone, camera, Touch ID, ports, lid sensor, ambient light sensor and keyboard backlight. Results are exported as a PDF and JSON report, with a share button and an offline QR code summary. Missing or skipped values are shown as "Not available" or "Not tested" rather than green or failed. The interface is offered in 18 languages.
use_cases: check a used Mac before buying it
document a Mac's condition before selling it
detect Activation Lock or MDM blockers on a second-hand Mac
check battery cycles and SSD health
test screen, keyboard, trackpad and ports of a used laptop
send a condition report PDF to a buyer
how_to_run: Download the DMG from the latest release
Drag Aman Check into the Applications folder
Open the app and follow the macOS Gatekeeper steps (Open Anyway, or xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine on the app)
Build from source: ./build_app.sh (or UNIVERSAL=1 ./build_app.sh for a universal binary)
stack: Cloudflare Workers, Hono, D1 (planned online publishing server in server/)
notable: Entirely local at level 1: no network connection, no telemetry, no update check
Reads only; asks for no administrator password and changes nothing on the checked Mac
Serial number never shown in full (last 4 characters only)
Report wording is deliberately cautious: no grade, no score, no 'certified' claims
Adapts tests to the model: Touch Bar, Touch ID, headphone jack and similar tests appear only when the Mac has them
caveats: Not signed with a paid Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks the first launch and requires a manual workaround
Developed and verified only on an Intel MacBook Pro with a T2 chip; some Apple Silicon and desktop sensor readings are not yet verified
Online verifiable publishing (level 2) is not deployed and is hidden in the app
